"""Semantic version parsing, comparison, and range matching.

Versions follow Semantic Versioning 2.0.0: ``MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH``, then an
optional pre-release (``-`` followed by dot-separated identifiers) and an
optional build (``+`` followed by dot-separated identifiers). Identifiers
are non-empty and made of ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens. Numeric parts
(MAJOR, MINOR, PATCH, and all-digit pre-release identifiers) must not have
leading zeros. Anything else is invalid and raises ``ValueError``.

Precedence (``compare``) follows the SemVer 2.0.0 rules: compare MAJOR,
MINOR, and PATCH numerically; a version with a pre-release is lower than
the same version without one; pre-release identifiers are compared left to
right, all-digit ones numerically and the rest in ASCII order, with
all-digit identifiers lower than the rest, and a shorter list lower when
all its identifiers equal the start of a longer one. Build metadata is
ignored.

Ranges (``satisfies``) are one or more comparator sets joined by ``||``; a
version satisfies the range if it satisfies any set. A set is one or more
comparators separated by whitespace, all of which must hold. A comparator
is a full version optionally prefixed by an operator:

- ``=`` (or no operator), ``>``, ``>=``, ``<``, ``<=``: by precedence.
- ``^X.Y.Z``: at least ``X.Y.Z`` and below the next version that changes
  the leftmost non-zero part, i.e. ``^1.2.3`` is ``>=1.2.3 <2.0.0``,
  ``^0.2.3`` is ``>=0.2.3 <0.3.0``, and ``^0.0.3`` is ``>=0.0.3 <0.0.4``.
- ``~X.Y.Z``: at least ``X.Y.Z`` and below ``X.(Y+1).0``.

A version with a pre-release satisfies a set only if some comparator in
that set has a pre-release on the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (so
``1.2.3-beta.2`` satisfies ``>=1.2.3-beta.1`` but not ``>=1.0.0``).
Invalid ranges raise ``ValueError``.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

    major: int
    minor: int
    patch: int
    prerelease: tuple[str, ...] = ()

        raise NotImplementedError

    """Parse a version string."""
    raise NotImplementedError


def compare(a: str | Version, b: str | Version) -> int:
    """Return -1, 0, or 1 as ``a`` has lower, equal, or higher precedence."""
    raise NotImplementedError


def satisfies(version: str | Version, range_: str) -> bool:

Versions follow Semantic Versioning 2.0.0: ``MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH``, then an
optional pre-release (``-`` followed by dot-separated identifiers) and an
optional build (``+`` followed by dot-separated identifiers). Identifiers
are non-empty and made of ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens. Numeric parts
(MAJOR, MINOR, PATCH, and all-digit pre-release identifiers) must not have
leading zeros. Anything else is invalid and raises ``ValueError``.

Precedence (``compare``) follows the SemVer 2.0.0 rules: compare MAJOR,
MINOR, and PATCH numerically; a version with a pre-release is lower than
the same version without one; pre-release identifiers are compared left to
right, all-digit ones numerically and the rest in ASCII order, with
all-digit identifiers lower than the rest, and a shorter list lower when
all its identifiers equal the start of a longer one. Build metadata is
ignored.

Ranges (``satisfies``) are one or more comparator sets joined by ``||``; a
version satisfies the range if it satisfies any set. A set is one or more
comparators separated by whitespace, all of which must hold. A comparator

- ``=`` (or no operator), ``>``, ``>=``, ``<``, ``<=``: by precedence.

that set has a pre-release on the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (so

The script is at `/private/tmp/tmp5h_0pjxa/devkit_check.py`, outside the project. The project has no test suite, so I didn't add one. I can turn the script into a proper test suite if you like.

- **`semver`**: parsing, canonical `__str__`, comparison by SemVer 2.0.0 rules, and ranges with `||`, the comparison operators, `^` and `~`. A pre-release version only matches a range that names a pre-release of that same version.
- **`cron`**: five fields with lists, ranges, steps and month/day names. If both day fields are restricted, a day matching either one counts. A schedule that never fires (`0 0 30 2 *`) gives up after five years in under a millisecond.
- **`duration`**: strict parsing, canonical formatting (`PT0S` for zero; tiny fractions like `1e-7` come out as `PT0.0000001S`), and month addition that clamps the day (Jan 31 + 1 month → Feb 28/29).
- **`table`**: writes and reads tables with padding, alignment and `\|` escaping; reading tolerates missing outer pipes.
- **`ini`**: sections, keys, continuation lines and comments, plus recursive `${key}` / `${section:key}` / `$$` substitution that catches loops and missing references.

The docstrings didn't settle a few cases, so I chose:

- **Strict input:** no surrounding whitespace is allowed in versions or durations, and `>= 1.2.3` (with a space) is an invalid range. An empty range is also an error, because the docstring requires at least one comparator. npm would treat an empty range as "any version".
- **`^0.0.0`:** this means `>=0.0.0 <0.0.1`.
- **Aware datetimes in `duration.add`:** hours, minutes and seconds are added as real elapsed time, so across a clock change 24 hours can land at 13:00 on the next day. Python's default for aware datetimes would add clock time instead.
- **`duration.format`** raises `ValueError` for negative fields, because ISO 8601 can't express them.
- **`ini` edge cases:**
  - `[]` is accepted as a section with an empty name.
  - An unclosed `${` is left as literal text, like any other `$`.
  - In `${a:b:c}`, the last colon separates the section from the key, since keys can't contain colons.
- **Line splitting:** `ini` and `table` only break lines at `\n`, `\r\n` and `\r`. Python's `splitlines()` also breaks at characters such as form feeds, which would make error line numbers wrong.
